Section 6 • \(P\)3D with the discrete Fourier transform

6.5 Reduction to \(\mu\) wedges, \(\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}[b]\rvert_{\mu\in(\mu_1,\mu_2)}\)

Each grid mode has a definite modulus and direction, \(k[\vec{p},q]=\sqrt{|\vec{k}_\perp[\vec{p}]|^2+\mathcal{J}^2k_\parallel[q]^2}\) and \(\mu[\vec{p},q]=\mathcal{J}k_\parallel[q]/k[\vec{p},q]\), and the solid-angle integral of Eq. (5.10) becomes an average over the modes in the wedge: \begin{equation} \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}[b]\Big\rvert_{\mu\in(\mu_1,\mu_2)} \equiv \frac{1}{N_{b,\mu}} \sum_{\substack{(\vec{p},q)\,:\,k[\vec{p},q]\in b\\ \mu[\vec{p},q]\in(\mu_1,\mu_2)}} \widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}[\vec{p},q]. \tag{6.10} \end{equation} The \(\vec{k}=\vec{0}\) mode, with undefined \(\mu\), is excluded. In comoving units the grid spacings are \(k_{\rm f,\perp}\) and \(\mathcal{J}k_{\rm f,\parallel}=2\pi\mathcal{J}/L_\Lambda\), equal only if \(L_\Lambda=\mathcal{J}L_\perp\) (e.g. the spectral extent of a cubic simulation box): otherwise the grid is anisotropic, and the number of modes per wedge depends on \(\mu\) even at fixed \(k\). At low \(k\) only a few discrete values of \(\mu\) are available, so the wedges are sparsely and unevenly populated. For \((\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-1,1)\) all the modes in the shell are averaged, and the imaginary parts cancel in pairs \((\vec{p},q),(-\vec{p},-q)\), as in Eq. (5.11).
